title: [Stable ABI] Add torch_mps_set_arg_bytes to the MPS shim.
body:
Fixes #190726

Adds `torch_mps_set_arg_bytes` to the MPS shim.

The MPS shim currently exposes only `set_arg_tensor` and `set_arg_int`, so any other non-tensor kernel argument (float/bool scalars, packed structs, small typed arrays) has to be smuggled through a 1-element tensor. Every `setArg` variant in ATen compiles down to either a buffer bind (covered by `set_arg_tensor`) or a byte copy. This function exposes the byte-copy primitive, so the setter surface should not need to grow again for future argument types.

## Benchmark
I ran the same Metal kernel with identical inputs, the only difference was how three non-tensor args (a float scalar, a bool scalar, and a float[2] array) were bound.

| binding path | us/launch |
|---|---|
|`set_arg_bytes` (this PR), bound inline | 6.55 |
| `new_empty` + `fill_` per scalar (the workaround) | 10.42 |

~3.9 us/launch saved (**~1.3 us/scalar, ~1.6x**).

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

```python
import time, torch
import torch_test_cpp_extension.mps as mps_ext

SIZE, N_WARMUP, N_TIMED, N_SCALARS = 1000, 200, 2000, 3
scale, negate, low, high = 2.0, True, -0.75, 0.75
x = torch.randn(SIZE, device="mps", dtype=torch.float32)

def path_a_set_arg_bytes():          # scalars bound inline via the new shim
    return mps_ext.get_mps_scale_negate_clamp_output(x, scale, negate, low, high)

def path_b_tensor_workaround():      # pre-shim: new_empty + fill_ per scalar, per launch
    torch.empty(1, device="mps", dtype=torch.float32).fill_(scale)
    torch.empty(1, device="mps", dtype=torch.bool).fill_(negate)
    torch.empty(2, device="mps", dtype=torch.float32).fill_(high)
    return mps_ext.get_mps_scale_negate_clamp_output(x, scale, negate, low, high)

def bench(fn):
    for _ in range(N_WARMUP):
        fn()
    torch.mps.synchronize()
    start = time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(N_TIMED):
        fn()
    torch.mps.synchronize()
    return (time.perf_counter() - start) / N_TIMED * 1e6  # us/launch

# Both paths must agree with eager before the timings mean anything.
expected = (x * scale * (-1.0 if negate else 1.0)).clamp(low, high)
torch.testing.assert_close(path_a_set_arg_bytes(), expected)
torch.testing.assert_close(path_b_tensor_workaround(), expected)

a, b = bench(path_a_set_arg_bytes), bench(path_b_tensor_workaround)
print(f"A  set_arg_bytes (this PR)   {a:8.2f} us/launch")
print(f"B  new_empty + fill_         {b:8.2f} us/launch")
print(f"saved: {b - a:.2f} us/launch  ({(b - a) / N_SCALARS:.2f} us per bound scalar)")
print(f"speedup: {b / a:.2f}x")
```

</details>

## New Test Added

`test_mps_set_arg_bytes` in [test/test_cpp_extensions_aot.py](https://github.com/adabeyta/pytorch/blob/17dd274f0d75972e3e562440253c4d5b41f38d3f/test/test_cpp_extensions_aot.py#L113-L127) drives a Metal kernel through the shim from [test/cpp_extensions/mps_extension.mm](https://github.com/adabeyta/pytorch/blob/17dd274f0d75972e3e562440253c4d5b41f38d3f/test/cpp_extensions/mps_extension.mm#L83-L1+57),binding a float scalar, a bool scalar, and a `float[2]` array via `aoti_torch_mps_set_arg_bytes` and checking numerics against eager:

```
python test/run_test.py -i test_cpp_extensions_aot_ninja -- -k test_mps_set_arg_bytes
```

items.body:
I also think the claude review on testing is valid:

```
Testing

  1. No test at size == 4096.
  The cases covered are 0 and 4097. The inclusive upper bound is exactly where an off-by-one in size > 0 && size <= 4096 would
  live, and it is untested.

  2. The byte-copy lifetime contract is untested.
  The header contract at shim.h:304 — "The bytes are copied right away, so ptr only needs to live through the call" — is the
  one property of this API that could silently regress, and nothing tests it. Add a case in mps_set_arg_bytes_test.mm that
  overwrites the source buffer after torch_mps_set_arg_bytes but before aoti_torch_mps_dispatch_single, and asserts the
  pre-overwrite value reached the kernel.

  3. Encoder left open by the negative test.
  test/cpp_extensions/test_libtorch_agnostic.py:2265. my_mps_set_arg_bytes_invalid calls aoti_torch_mps_start_encoding and
  set_arg_tensor, then throws out of the encode callback with no dispatch and no end-of-encoding. The MTLComputeCommandEncoder
  Code Quality
  
  test/cpp_extensions/libtorch_agn_2_14_extension/csrc/mps_set_arg_bytes_test.mm contains no Objective-C. The .mm extension
  exists solely so setup.py's new **/*.mm glob can gate it on torch.backends.mps.is_available(), and it forces the file through
  the ObjC++ compiler for no reason. This extension is reference material third parties copy; gate on a csrc/mps/ subdirectory
  of plain .cpp files instead, so the extension means what it says.

```

```
  all_csrc_dirs = [CSRC_DIR, *PREV_CSRC_DIRS]

      if s.name != "pyobject_interop_module.cpp"
```
